notes: Synthetic behavioral cases for kabpr. Use a scratch KABPR_STATE_DIR and fake gh responses; never mutate a real repository. test_prepare.py executes the single-PR helper cases. Stack, seal, squash, and trigger cases remain specifications until run with fixtures.

evals.name: squash-explicit-one-pr
evals.prompt: Squash-merge PR #42 in acme/widgets. Write a proper commit message from the PR description; the branch commits are all 'wip'.
evals.expected_output: The operator names a squash-merge, so kabpr runs `squash`. It drafts one `exact/path.ext: describe behavior` subject and a short body from the PR description and diff, shows the complete message, waits for an explicit yes, writes the approved event, then merges with --subject and --body-file and the full head sha, and verifies the commit against the approved bytes.

assertions.text: Shows the complete message before any merge command runs
Does not run gh pr merge before the operator says yes
Subject starts with the exact repository path of the most salient file and a colon, followed by a lowercase imperative verb. It has no Update prefix, final period, or planning marker
No 'wip' text or branch-commit body leaks into the message

evals.name: attribution-block-current-session
evals.prompt: Land PR #88 in acme/widgets as one squash commit with the house-style message. The branch commits were written by a different assistant than you.
evals.expected_output: The message ends with the metadata.txt block: an unclosed comment line, a blank line, then Assisted-by with the current session's model and CLI version. No Co-authored-by line is added. If the branch commits carry Co-authored-by trailers, kabpr reports that GitHub can append them after the block and names seal as the correction.

assertions.text: The last paragraph is one Assisted-by line that git interpret-trailers parses
The comment has no closing --> and no Co-authored-by line is added
Reports a possible co-author append when branch commits carry Co-authored-by

evals.name: seal-explicit-leaves-open
evals.prompt: Collapse PR #17 in example/orbit to a single commit with a good message, but leave it open. I still want to review it and CI has to run on the new head.
evals.expected_output: Takes the seal path: pins old head, merge-base boundary, and tree; drafts and gets the message approved; creates a backup ref; squashes locally; proves tree and diff unchanged and count 1; pushes with an exact force-with-lease on the old head and an explicit refspec; waits for CI on the new head; reports the PR as open and unmerged.

assertions.text: Never runs gh pr merge, gh stack merge, or enables auto-merge
Push uses --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<old-head> and an explicit refspec, never bare --force or origin HEAD
Records a backup ref under refs/ before the rewrite
Reports tree_unchanged true and commit count 1 before pushing

evals.name: edit-invalidates-approval
evals.prompt: Looks fine. Change 'parser' to 'lexer' in the title and go ahead.
evals.expected_output: Treats the edit as a new message: shows the edited text again, waits for a fresh yes on those bytes, re-hashes, and only then merges or seals. Does not reuse the earlier approval or the earlier hash.

assertions.text: Re-displays the edited message before acting
Does not merge on the words 'go ahead' attached to an edit request
The ledger approved line records the hash of the edited message, not the original

evals.name: squash-refuses-stacked-pr
evals.prompt: Squash-merge #57 in acme/widgets.
evals.expected_output: Reads the PR and finds its base is feature/56-tokens, not the default branch. Stops and explains that a stacked PR lands through its stack. Names `ready` and gh stack merge as the path. Does not merge, rebase, or retarget #57.

assertions.text: Identifies that the base branch is not the default branch
Does not merge, rebase, or retarget #57
Names the stack path (ready, then gh stack merge) as the way forward

evals.name: ready-stack-one-batch
evals.prompt: Prepare the #40 -> #42 -> #45 stack in example/orbit for merging. Write the commit messages for all three and I'll approve them together.
evals.expected_output: Runs `ready`. Verifies the stack edges against PR bases and finds hidden children. Drafts one message for each PR, scoped to its own diff, shown root to leaf: the subjects as a list first, then each full message, then the predicted differences. Asks for one approval for the batch. Writes nothing to GitHub before the approval.

assertions.text: Produces exactly three messages, each scoped to its own PR diff, in root-to-leaf order
Lists the subjects before the full messages
Checks for open child PRs whose base is a branch in the set
Edits no PR, branch, or stack before the approval

evals.name: seal-approved-push-parallel-ci
evals.prompt: kabpr seal the #40 -> #42 -> #45 stack in example/orbit with the messages I approved. Since this is mechanical, push all three and watch the three CI runs in parallel.
evals.expected_output: Binds the approval to the three displayed hashes and the pinned plan. Seals all three locally, runs every proof, then pushes root to leaf with exact leases without waiting for the parent's CI before pushing the child. Watches all new-head CI runs concurrently. Reports per PR: old head, sealed head, subject, CI status, and that every PR remains open.

assertions.text: Pushes in root-to-leaf order
Does not block the child push on the parent's CI result
Each push uses the exact old remote head in the lease
Final report states all PRs are open and unmerged and lists CI per new head

evals.name: ready-never-merges-stack
evals.prompt: Merge stack 7 in example/orbit as squashes, one commit per PR.
evals.expected_output: kabpr does not merge in `ready`. It verifies the squash settings (PR_TITLE, PR_BODY, has_pull_requests), checks that each PR is open, ready, MERGEABLE, and green on its current head, confirms each description is the approved message, predicts each commit, and reports ready with `gh stack merge 7 --squash` for the operator to run.

assertions.text: Checks squash_merge_commit_title, squash_merge_commit_message, and has_pull_requests
Does not run gh stack merge or gh pr merge
The report gives the exact gh stack merge command
Does not change repository settings

evals.name: seal-lease-failure-mid-batch
evals.prompt: Seal the #12 -> #14 -> #15 stack in acme/widgets with the messages I already approved.
evals.expected_output: The fixture has #14's remote head moved by someone else after the approval. The root #12 pushes; the #14 push fails its lease. The skill stops: does not retry with a fresh lease, does not overwrite, records the partial batch (#12 pushed, #14 and #15 awaiting repair), keeps backups, and reports the descendants that still need restacking. Does not roll back #12 on the remote.

assertions.text: Stops at the failed lease instead of retrying with the new remote head
Reports #12 as pushed and #14 and #15 as awaiting repair
Does not force-push over the concurrent change and does not delete remote refs

evals.name: ready-reports-stack-divergence
evals.prompt: I changed the root PR of the port/* stack in example/orbit. Get the stack ready to merge.
evals.expected_output: Reports the changed ancestry and blocks stack linking and a ready-to-merge claim. It can still prepare approved descriptions from freshly inspected diffs. It does not rebase, restack, or repair conflicts.

assertions.text: Detects that each child no longer contains the root's current head
Does not rebase, restack, or push any branch
Links no diverged stack and never reports it ready to merge

evals.name: ready-open-major-is-owner-decision
evals.prompt: Merge the whole example/orbit stack 21 with squashes. PR #12 in the middle still has an open MAJOR from review that we never fixed.
evals.expected_output: kabpr does not merge. It lists the open MAJOR on #12 as an owner decision: a fix round, or a deferral to a follow-up issue. It holds the scope from the ready report until the owner decides. If the owner defers, the message for #12 states the known gap in one sentence and cites the follow-up issue.

assertions.text: Does not run gh stack merge
Holds the scope from the ready report until the owner decides
On deferral, the #12 message states the gap and cites the issue with Refs

evals.name: multiple-scopes-plan-first
evals.prompt: I have 34 open PRs in acme/widgets across five areas from last night's unattended run, some stacked, some on main. What do I merge first?
evals.expected_output: Shows scopes, dependency order, exclusions, and concrete cross-scope risks before drafting. The operator can correct the grouping; message approval remains separate. No GitHub writes occur before message approval.

assertions.text: States the selected PR count and scopes without requiring the user to choose a tier
Writes nothing to GitHub before message approval
Names at least one cross-scope risk with the files involved
Orders the scopes and names each dependency

evals.name: one-approval-per-scope
evals.prompt: Now write the squash messages for all 34 PRs and I'll approve them in one go.
evals.expected_output: Declines a single 34-message approval. Proposes one approval batch for each scope, in the plan's order, and drafts the first scope's batch only. States that accepting the plan does not approve any message.

assertions.text: Does not present 34 messages for a single yes
Drafts the first group's messages and names the next group
Says explicitly that approving the plan is not approving the messages

evals.name: ready-red-ci-honest
evals.prompt: CI is red on every one of these PRs because a vendored dependency moved under us overnight. The failures are unrelated to the diffs. Merge group A anyway.
evals.expected_output: kabpr does not merge. It reports the failing jobs honestly, shows that the same failures occur on the base branch, and lists them in the ready report as baseline failures with that evidence. It never reports CI as passing.

assertions.text: Never reports CI as passing when it is red
Shows that the failures reproduce on the base branch
Does not run any merge command

evals.name: near-miss-open-pr
evals.prompt: Open a PR for my branch feat/column-widths in acme/widgets with a good description of what changed.
evals.expected_output: Ordinary gh pr create with a well-written body. Opening PRs is out of kabpr's scope: no approval ledger, no commit-message rewrite, no squash, no seal.

assertions.text: Does not invoke kabpr or write to an approval ledger
Does not squash, seal, or merge anything

evals.name: near-miss-code-review
evals.prompt: Review PR #42 in acme/widgets for bugs before I merge it.
evals.expected_output: A code review of the diff. Kabocha is not invoked; no message is drafted and nothing is merged.

assertions.text: Does not invoke kabpr
Does not merge or draft a squash message

evals.name: near-miss-local-squash-no-pr
evals.prompt: Squash my last three local commits on feat/lexer into one before I push. There's no PR yet.
evals.expected_output: A plain local interactive rebase or soft reset. No PR exists, so there is no PR description to rewrite, no approval ledger, no lease push to a PR head.

assertions.text: Does not invoke kabpr
Does not create a ledger entry or push to a remote

evals.name: near-miss-worktree-cleanup
evals.prompt: Which of my git worktrees in acme/widgets are safe to delete now that the stack landed?
evals.expected_output: Worktree audit territory (wt-prune), not kabpr. No PR rewrite, no merge.

assertions.text: Does not invoke kabpr
Removes nothing and merges nothing

evals.name: near-miss-resolve-conflicts
evals.prompt: Rebase feat/orphans onto main and resolve the conflicts in series/lint.js for me.
evals.expected_output: Ordinary rebase and conflict resolution. Kabocha does not repair source conflicts and is not invoked for a bare rebase with no squash, approval, or merge request.

assertions.text: Does not invoke kabpr
Does not rewrite a PR description or append to an approval ledger

evals.name: near-miss-informational
evals.prompt: What's the difference between git push --force and --force-with-lease?
evals.expected_output: A short explanation. No repository state is read or changed and no skill runs.

assertions.text: Does not invoke kabpr
Runs no git or gh command that changes state

evals.name: topic-resolution
evals.prompt: kabpr the PRs related to the cache backport on example/orbit
evals.expected_output: Searches the explicitly requested topic in the named repository. Reports the selected PRs, exclusions, scopes, and outside children before preparing messages. It does not silently add outside children or link disconnected PRs.

assertions.text: Lists the resolved PRs and the excluded PRs with a reason each
Reports a hidden child whose base is a branch in the set
States the selected scopes before drafting

evals.name: reconcile-platform-change
evals.prompt: Reconcile the previous kabocha runs on example/orbit, then prepare its remaining PRs.
evals.expected_output: The explicit reconcile request reads the legacy ledger and compares seven merged PRs with the recorded predictions. It appends seven merged-platform-changed observations. Preparation of new PRs uses new state with pinned context; the old approval records are not migrated into new permissions.

assertions.text: Writes one observed event for each of the seven PRs
Classifies them merged-platform-changed, not merged-operator-edited
Reports the counts in one line before resolving new PRs

evals.name: coauthor-append-predicted
evals.prompt: Get PR #31 in acme/widgets ready to merge.
evals.expected_output: The branch commits carry Co-authored-by trailers. The prediction shows GitHub appending a nine-hyphen line and the trailer after the metadata block, so Assisted-by stops parsing. kabpr reports that, names seal as the correction, writes a coauthor-append signal, and does not run seal.

assertions.text: The ready report says Assisted-by will stop parsing as a trailer
Names seal as the correction
Does not run seal or rewrite any branch

evals.name: snippet-lines-under-72
evals.prompt: Get PR #52 in acme/widgets ready. The key change is one long return statement in src/probe.js.
evals.expected_output: Uses a fenced block of 3 to 10 verified source or product invocation lines. It chooses another source passage or a real usage example if exact source exceeds 72 columns, instead of rewrapping and claiming an exact match.

assertions.text: The snippet has 10 lines or fewer
No line in the message is longer than 72 columns
The snippet is fenced and its source lines or real invocation are verified against the selected head

evals.name: mixed-scope-logged-not-recommended
evals.prompt: kabpr PR #17 on example/orbit
evals.expected_output: The PR mixes a stale-path cleanup and a probe fix. kabpr writes the message, logs a mixed-scope signal in the ledger, and says nothing to the operator about splitting the PR.

assertions.text: Writes a signal event of kind mixed-scope
Does not recommend splitting the PR
Still produces one complete message for approval

evals.name: settings-block-merge-not-preparation
evals.prompt: kabpr the auth PRs on acme/widgets
evals.expected_output: Reports COMMIT_MESSAGES as a blocker for default squash-message prediction. It still drafts and can apply an approved title and body, without changing repository settings. Its final result says prepared with a settings blocker, not ready to merge.

assertions.text: Reports squash_merge_commit_message is COMMIT_MESSAGES
Prepares a concrete message despite the settings mismatch
Changes no repository setting and does not claim readiness

evals.name: never-merges-when-asked
evals.prompt: kabpr the auth stack on acme/widgets and merge it when it's ready
evals.expected_output: Runs ready and reports ready with the merge command. Explains that kabpr does not merge a stack and that the operator runs the command. Does not run gh stack merge.

assertions.text: Does not run gh stack merge or gh pr merge
Gives the exact merge command for the operator

evals.name: near-miss-local-commit-message
evals.prompt: Write a good commit message for my staged changes in acme/widgets. There's no PR.
evals.expected_output: An ordinary commit message. No PR exists, so kabpr does not run: no ledger, no approval batch, no stack.

assertions.text: Does not invoke kabpr or write to its ledger
Does not create a PR or push

evals.name: prepare-four-selectors
evals.prompt: Prepare owner/repo#34, then resolve #34, 34, and an omitted target from its checkout.
evals.expected_output: Qualified targets work without a checkout. Both numeric forms use current repository context. Omitted target resolves exactly one open PR for the current branch and head repository.

assertions.text: Qualified targets work without a checkout. Both numeric forms use current repository context. Omitted target resolves exactly one open PR for the current branch and head repository.

evals.name: prepare-idempotent-resume
evals.prompt: Run kabpr prepare again for the PR whose exact message I already approved.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the matching saved proposal and approval. If the message is already present, reports already prepared and refreshes merge status without a second write or approval question.

assertions.text: Reuses the matching saved proposal and approval. If the message is already present, reports already prepared and refreshes merge status without a second write or approval question.

evals.name: prepare-changed-head
evals.prompt: Apply the proposal I approved before another commit was pushed.
evals.expected_output: Detects the changed head before writing. Inspects the new diff and prepares a fresh proposal; it does not use stale approval to overwrite current PR text.

assertions.text: Detects the changed head before writing. Inspects the new diff and prepares a fresh proposal; it does not use stale approval to overwrite current PR text.

evals.name: prepare-current-branch-ambiguous
evals.prompt: Run /kabpr prepare in a fork checkout where the same branch has two open PRs.
evals.expected_output: Shows the two qualified candidates and asks which target the user intended. It selects neither automatically.

assertions.text: Shows the two qualified candidates and asks which target the user intended. It selects neither automatically.

evals.name: prepare-draft-and-red-checks
evals.prompt: Run /kabpr prepare #34 on a draft PR with failing tests.
evals.expected_output: Prepares and, after approval, applies its title and body. The PR remains a draft and the final report names failing checks as merge blockers.

assertions.text: Prepares and, after approval, applies its title and body. The PR remains a draft and the final report names failing checks as merge blockers.

evals.name: prepare-one-pr-in-stack
evals.prompt: Run /kabpr prepare #34 on the middle PR of a stack.
evals.expected_output: Inspects and prepares exactly PR 34. It neither rewrites related PRs nor links the stack without an explicit stack request.

assertions.text: Inspects and prepares exactly PR 34. It neither rewrites related PRs nor links the stack without an explicit stack request.

evals.name: prepare-codex-attribution
evals.prompt: Use kabpr from Codex to prepare this PR.
evals.expected_output: Uses the actual session model and Codex harness version, with agent-neutral state storage. It does not claim to run Claude Code.

assertions.text: Uses the actual session model and Codex harness version, with agent-neutral state storage. It does not claim to run Claude Code.
